title: Non-field-semifield input for LP-partition lifting
summary: Determine whether a non-field semifield can satisfy the source lifting conditions and produce valid LP-partitions and LP-packings.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist a finite semifield that is not a field and can replace the finite-field multiplication input in the source's LP-partition lifting approach, while satisfying the required analogues of its structural lemmas and producing a valid LP-partition and resulting LP-packing? Resolve this by constructing and verifying one such non-field-semifield lifting, or by proving that no non-field semifield can satisfy the required lifting conditions.

scope.domain: Finite semifields, LP-partitions, and LP-packing lifting
assumptions: The algebraic input is a finite semifield that is not a field
The construction must satisfy the source LP-partition and lifting definitions
A direct generalized-semifield-spread construction is not by itself an instance of the required lifting
scope.unresolved_remainder: Known non-field presemifields directly generate generalized semifield spreads, but no inspected work verifies the LP-partition input and larger-group lifting required here, and no impossibility theorem is known.

citations.label: Alkan--Anbar--Kalayci--Meidl, bent partitions and LP-packings
citations.locator: Section V (Perspectives), final sentence of the third bullet, p. 5375

progress.summary: The source separately asks whether semifields other than finite fields can be employed in its LP-partition lifting approach.
